thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: geo-steer anomaly detected — sustained cross-region traffic spike from us-west1 -> eu-west2 (service: inference-api). Errors + latency rising. Alert id=GEO-STEER-7723

sam: Ack. I'm oncall. Triage started. Paging @net-team and @infra. Any quick customer impact numbers?

nina: Seeing a ~12% increase in p95 (now 1.1s) and error rate from 0.3% -> 4.8% for inference-api across the last 6m. Traffic to eu-west2 jumped ~27% from us-west1 origin.

alex: Might be related to the routing-policy refactor merged 22m ago (PR #4567). That change altered weight computation and TTL handling for region pins.

sam: Good call. @alex can you confirm if that PR touched steering fallback logic?

alex: Yes — it adjusts pin aging and fallthrough. Quick grep shows the fallback comparator was swapped; tests passed locally but didn't cover mixed TTLs.

miguel: Customer-impact note: CS reported higher latency and some 502s from two Nordic customers on EU edge. Ticket INC-998 opened.

customer-success: Confirmed — a 3rd party partner (payment-gateway) reported timeouts. They've temporarily routed traffic to our eu endpoints and are seeing 1–2s extra latency. We're communicating that team is actively mitigating.

sam: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pin override to prefer us-west1 for affected origin prefixes, 2) rollback the routing-policy change (if necessary) as a safety, 3) raise TTL on geo response to avoid flapping while we fix. Who can run pin override ASAP?

alex: I can push a manual pin override. Command (redwoodctl):

```
redwoodctl routing pin create --origin-prefix us-west1 --region us-west1 --reason "emergency pin for GEO-STEER-7723" --expires-in 1h
```

sam: Run it and post the change id. Also add a short description for audit.

alex: Done. Pin created id=pin-20260315-9f3c, expires in 60m. net-bot: please validate propagation.

net-bot: Pin id=pin-20260315-9f3c accepted. Propagation kicked to edge controllers, expected effect within 30–60s per region.

(30s later)

nina: Metrics: requests to eu-west2 from affected prefixes dropped 23% in the last 45s; p95 across origins improving to ~680ms. Error rate down to 1.1%.

sam: Nice. That's breathing room. Now run safety rollback plan for PR #4567. @tess can you coordinate a rollback deploy to staging then prod? Keep a canary.

tess: On it. Rolling back the routing-policy refactor — initiating canary in us-west1 with 5% traffic. Command:

```
ci deploy rollback --ref PR-4567 --env canary --target inference-routing --percent 5
```

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline started for rollback (job id=deploy-8921). Canary will run for 10m with synthetic checks.

(10m)

tess: Canary looks clean. Synthetic latencies stable, no errors. Rolling full rollback to prod now.

infra-bot: Prod rollback complete (job id=deploy-8921, status=SUCCESS).

alex: After rollback, confirmed the weight computation reverted. Also increasing geo TTL for the problematic prefixes to 300s to avoid immediate re-flapping. Command used:

```
redwoodctl routing update --origin-prefix us-west1 --geo-ttl 300 --note "temporary TTL increase during recovery"
```

net-bot: Geo TTL update accepted. DNS fans out within configured ~60s.

nina: Post-rollback metrics: p95 steady ~420ms, error rate 0.2% — back to baseline. Cross-region traffic to eu-west2 normalized.

sam: Confirmed. Incident severity reduced. Customer-impacted tickets updated. @customer-success please relay recovery note and ETA for postmortem.

customer-success: Messaging drafted and sent to payment-gateway and affected Nordic customers. Will follow up with postmortem once triage complete.

miguel: Any external vendor involved? We saw no BGP shifts; looks internal to our steering logic.

alex: Agreed. Root cause hypothesis: PR #4567 introduced a comparator sign flip for pin aging in the fallback path. Under mixed TTL scenarios, late-arriving lighter-weight route triggered fallthrough to a farther region.

sam: Actions captured for follow-up: 1) Postmortem with timeline and root cause, 2) Add unit/integration tests for mixed TTL steer cases, 3) Add synthetic canary for geo-steadiness after routing changes, 4) Improve alerting to show pin conflicts + recent routing PRs.

tess: I'll own the rollback runbook updates and add a checklist for pin overrides.

alex: I'll add tests and submit PR with fix + extra logging.

nina: I'll create dashboard panels to highlight origin->region heatmaps and pin mismatch alarms.

sam: Good. Handoff to next oncall @tess (until 08:00 UTC). Document any remaining watch items.

tess: Handoff ack. Current watch windows: increased geo-ttl expires in 45m (pin still active 15m). I'll monitor for re-flapping and follow up with devs.

infra-bot: NOTE: pin id=pin-20260315-9f3c expires in 15m — auto-expire will remove override.

sam: If pin still needed at expiry, extend or re-evaluate based on metrics. Otherwise let it expire and monitor.

(1h 4m after start)

nina: All green. No regression in last 30m. Marking incident as resolved in monitoring and updating incident tracker.

infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: GEO-STEER-7723 — root-cause: regression in routing-policy code (PR #4567). Postmortem scheduled.

sam: Thanks everyone for fast coordination. We'll do the blameless postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:

customer-success: Customers notified, will close tickets after confirmation.

miguel: Logging action: link to rollback commit and timeline added to the incident doc (INC-7723).

sam: Closing thread and handing to postmortem owners (alex, tess, nina). If anything else shows up ping me.

net-bot: Auto-summarize: pin override + rollback prevented further customer impact; rollback PR merged to fix comparator; TTL increase used as short-term stabilizer.
